assumptions: 'Success rate' means attempt-level success rate: successful attempts divided by all attempts, with each retry counted as a separate attempt. Order-level and technical rates are shown alongside.
The comparison is 18–31 Oct 2026 against 4–17 Oct 2026, the immediately preceding period of equal length.
caveats: Duplicate records on 12 Oct: 341 attempts were ingested twice (11,704 raw rows vs 11,363 unique attempts, +3.0%). Paysight counts each attempt once, keeping the first ingestion.

Attempt volume from 18 Oct to 31 Oct was about 39% above the usual level for those weekdays. A sale and a data gap look alike, so check before comparing totals across this period; it is not a data error by itself.
The success rate depends on the denominator: attempt-level 88.5%, order-level 90.9%, technical 92.1%. Retries and customer drop-offs explain the gap.
Failure codes are quoted per 100 attempts.
The daily series in the evidence for Harbor Bank debit cards covers only 4–15 Oct, so the exact start date of the Harbor Bank drop is not shown.

facts.text: Attempt success rate fell 1.47pp from 90.0% (148,791 of 165,297 attempts) to 88.5% (203,741 of 230,100 attempts). The change is statistically significant and practically significant.
By payment method, the 1.47pp fall splits into a mix effect of -1.00pp (68.0% of the change) and a like-for-like rate effect of -0.47pp.

CARD_EMI grew from 2.9% to 10.9% of attempts while its own rate stayed flat (81.7% to 81.6%), so it cost about -0.61pp through mix alone. UPI, the highest-success method, fell from 54.0% to 42.5% of attempts, costing about -0.43pp through mix.
NovaMart's share of volume rose from 6.0% to 30.0%. NovaMart accounts for -0.96pp (65%) of the -1.47pp change, and its own rate fell from 90.0% to 86.2%.
The largest like-for-like drop is Harbor Bank debit cards: the success rate fell from 86.2% to 76.7% (-9.44pp), contributing -0.39pp to the overall change.

For Harbor Bank debit cards, ISSUER_RISK_DECLINE rose from 0.32 to 11.12 failures per 100 attempts (1,065 failures in the current period vs 22 in the baseline). Other failure codes were broadly flat or lower.
Harbor Bank debit daily success rates ranged from 83.9% to 88.9% across 4–15 Oct; the daily series in the evidence covers only the baseline period, with no anomaly window flagged.
Other debit-card segments also declined (for example west | DEBIT_CARD from 85.9% to 83.3%, Meridian Bank | DEBIT_CARD from 85.7% to 83.0%), though their contributions are smaller than Harbor Bank's.

response.headline: Attempt success rate fell 1.47pp, from 90.0% to 88.5%, comparing 18–31 Oct with 4–17 Oct. About two-thirds is a shift in payment mix (more EMI and card volume, less UPI) and about one-third is a genuine like-for-like drop, concentrated in Harbor Bank debit cards.

hypotheses.how_to_verify: Check the merchant's campaign calendar and compare payment-method mix on NovaMart attempts before and after 18 Oct.
hypotheses.rationale: Attempt volume was up about 39% over the period, NovaMart's share rose five-fold, and CARD_EMI's share rose from 2.9% to 10.9% with a flat own rate.
hypotheses.text: A sale or campaign (for example at NovaMart) pushed volume toward EMI and card payments and away from UPI, which explains most of the headline decline as a mix shift rather than worse payment performance.

hypotheses.how_to_verify: Ask Harbor Bank whether risk or fraud rules changed around 18 Oct, and check the daily Harbor Bank debit rate and ISSUER_RISK_DECLINE counts across the current period.
hypotheses.rationale: The ISSUER_RISK_DECLINE rate rose from 0.32 to 11.12 per 100 attempts while other failure codes stayed flat or fell, pointing to an issuer-side risk decision rather than a technical fault.
hypotheses.text: Harbor Bank tightened or misconfigured its risk rules on debit cards, causing a surge in ISSUER_RISK_DECLINE.

hypotheses.how_to_verify: Compare customer, device and ticket-size profiles of Harbor Bank debit declines against baseline-period attempts.
hypotheses.rationale: Volume and the NovaMart share both rose sharply, and Harbor Bank's share of volume rose from 8.8% to 11.0%, but the evidence does not show who the extra traffic is.
hypotheses.text: The high-volume period may be drawing in riskier or atypical traffic that triggers more issuer risk declines.

recommendations.linked_fact_or_hypothesis: Harbor Bank tightened or misconfigured its risk rules on debit cards, causing a surge in ISSUER_RISK_DECLINE.
recommendations.rationale: This is the largest like-for-like drop (-9.44pp) and is driven by one failure code.
recommendations.text: Raise the ISSUER_RISK_DECLINE spike on Harbor Bank debit cards with the issuer and ask whether risk rules changed on or around 18 Oct.

recommendations.linked_fact_or_hypothesis: By payment method, the 1.47pp fall splits into a mix effect of -1.00pp (68.0% of the change) and a like-for-like rate effect of -0.47pp.
recommendations.rationale: About 68% of the decline is mix, so the headline rate overstates any deterioration in underlying performance.
recommendations.text: Report the success rate with and without the NovaMart sale traffic, and judge payment performance on like-for-like payment-method mix rather than the headline number.

recommendations.linked_fact_or_hypothesis: Other debit-card segments also declined (for example west | DEBIT_CARD from 85.9% to 83.3%, Meridian Bank | DEBIT_CARD from 85.7% to 83.0%), though their contributions are smaller than Harbor Bank's.
recommendations.rationale: Debit-card rates fell across several segments, not only Harbor Bank.
recommendations.text: Review the other debit-card segments (west, south, Meridian Bank) and NovaMart's own 3.8pp rate drop to see whether they share a cause with Harbor Bank.
